hints: Notice that propene is an alkene, so think about which type of reaction from a bromoalkane makes a C=C double bond.
Remember that hydroxide can do two different jobs, substitution to an alcohol in aqueous solution and elimination to an alkene in ethanol.
Pick the reagent that acts as a strong base to pull off a hydrogen from the next carbon, rather than as a nucleophile that replaces Br.
walkthrough:
**Spot the reaction type needed**

Great start, let's look at what we have and what we want. We start with $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ and we want $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$.

That means losing HBr and forming a double bond, so this is an elimination reaction, not substitution.

**Recall the elimination condition**

This is the key Cambridge rule to remember. Aqueous hydroxide favours nucleophilic substitution to an alcohol, while hot ethanolic hydroxide favours elimination to an alkene.

Elimination equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{OH}^- \text{(in ethanol)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Br}^-$$

**Choose the best reagent for propene**

Ethanolic sodium hydroxide provides concentrated $\text{OH}^-$ in a non-aqueous solvent, so it acts as a base, removes $\text{H}^+$ from C-2, and ejects $\text{Br}^-$ from C-1.

That gives the highest yield of propene, while the other reagents mainly give substitution products.

options.A: Ammonia acts as a nucleophile in nucleophilic substitution to give a primary amine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$. It does not cause elimination, so almost no propene is formed.
options.B: Aqueous potassium hydroxide gives nucleophilic substitution to the alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. Water favours substitution over elimination, so this is the classic trap if you forget aqueous versus ethanolic.
options.C: Potassium cyanide provides $\text{CN}^-$ which is a strong nucleophile for substitution to give the nitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$. This extends the carbon chain, it does not form an alkene.
options.D: Ethanolic sodium hydroxide favours elimination. $\text{OH}^-$ acts as a base, removes a hydrogen from C-2 and eliminates $\text{Br}^-$ to form $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$. This gives the highest yield of propene.
